title: Intraosseous or Intravenous Vascular Access for Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest
shortTitle: IVIO: easier access did not translate into more sustained ROSC
summary: IVIO randomized 1,506 adults with nontraumatic OHCA; 1,479 entered the primary analysis. Sustained ROSC occurred in 30% with IO-first versus 29% with IV-first access (RR 1.06; 95% CI 0.90–1.24; P=.49), despite greater two-attempt access success with IO.
whyItMatters: Supports separating technical access success from patient-centered benefit. The trial provides no basis for replacing feasible IV-first access routinely.
limitations: The primary endpoint was sustained ROSC; survival and neurologic estimates were less precise. Results concern initial access during nontraumatic adult OHCA.
population: Adults with nontraumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.
findings: Access success within two attempts: 92% versus 80%.
Favorable neurologic survival: 9% versus 8%; RR 1.16 (95% CI 0.83–1.62); prespecified adverse events were uncommon.
evidenceNotes: Historical backfill: first-online date verified from the PubMed electronic publication record. Abstract reviewed; full text unavailable. This is historical evidence, not a new 2026 publication.
